extraction.name: LongVid
extraction.description: LongVid is a large-scale long video instruction-tuning dataset introduced in the paper for long video model training. It comprises 114,228 long videos and 3,444,849 question-answering pairs across five task types, built from sources including Ego4D, HowTo100M, HD-VILA, and MiraData to support diverse long video scenarios.
extraction.creator: Xinhao Li; Yi Wang; Jiashuo Yu; Xiangyu Zeng; Yuhan Zhu; Haian Huang; Jianfei Gao; Kunchang Li; Yinan He; Chenting Wang; Yu Qiao; Yali Wang; Limin Wang
extraction.citeAs: Xinhao Li, Yi Wang, Jiashuo Yu, Xiangyu Zeng, Yuhan Zhu, Haian Huang, Jianfei Gao, Kunchang Li, Yinan He, Chenting Wang, Yu Qiao, Yali Wang, and Limin Wang. VideoChat-Flash: Hierarchical Compression for Long-Context Video Modeling. arXiv:2501.00574, 2025.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: LongVid was constructed by leveraging existing datasets including Ego4D, HowTo100M, HD-VILA, and MiraData, and by filtering consecutive segments that can be regrouped into long video sequences.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis; Manual Human Curator
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: The videos of LongVid are curated from 4 open-source video datasets: Ego4D, HowTo100M, HD-VILA, and MiraData. For data curation, the authors utilize existing high-quality short video captions from Panda-70M for HD-VILA, CosMo for HowTo100M, Ego4D-HCap for Ego4D, and the original high-quality captions provided in MiraData.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: To build LongVid, the authors generated dense event labels for each long video by using existing high-quality short video captions, filtering consecutive segments that can be regrouped into a long video sequence, constructing event labels with corresponding timestamps, directly using existing event-level annotations for some datasets, and extracting the major event from captions using an LLM for others; they then constructed long-video QA pairs based on video captions, event labels, and timestamps, and for the Multi-Hop Needle in a Video Haystack benchmark they inserted reasoning paths composed of multiple images into videos using MS-COCO human-annotated captions and question-answer pairs.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Compression of visual content inevitably leads to the loss of detailed information; Previous NIAH-Video evaluation can suffer from information leakage and is insufficient for assessing complex reasoning ability
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: LongVid is built from datasets including Ego4D, which contains egocentric videos; the MH-NIAH-Video benchmark uses images sourced from MS-COCO with human-annotated captions and question-answer pairs.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: long-context video modeling in multimodal large language models; processing movies, documentaries, and online video streams; video captioning; temporal grounding; event relation recognition; scene relation recognition; video event counting
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: For Single-Hop NIAH, they source a long video, sample frames uniformly from it, then add needles (indicating images) into the sampled image sequence at different positions. For Multi-Hop NIAH, they insert a reasoning path composed of multiple images into the video haystack, with each image having a random insertion position and textual clues, and they also insert multiple wrong reasoning paths simultaneously while inserting the correct reasoning path.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: To build LongVid, they filter the consecutive segments that can be regroup into a long video sequence, then construct a sequence of event labels with their corresponding timestamps for every long video based on their captions; for some datasets they directly use existing event-level annotations as event labels, while for others they extract the major event from the caption using an LLM. For HD-VILA, they filter consecutive video segments that can be re-constructed into more than 60s long videos.
